label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Handover for Inês: launch Thursday 26 November

Inês,

My father is ill and I am with my family. I am leaving tonight and I don't know yet for how long, so the launch on Thursday is yours.

I am sorry to do this to you three days before. I am even more sorry about what I found this afternoon, because it means I am not handing you a finished launch, I am handing you a correction to make. The error is mine, not yours. If anyone asks, please say so in exactly those words.

I am not worried about Thursday. You know this paper as well as I do. The order below is only my suggestion. If you see a better way, do it your way; you don't need to check with me first.

You can call me. Tonight is fine. Tomorrow (Tuesday) from 9 in the morning I may not pick up, so leave a message or write and I will come back to you when I can.

THE ERROR

Figure 3 and the summary used the 2030 revenue estimate from the old run, where the free allocation phase-out was not applied. The correct number for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does. My note from this afternoon is in this folder.

Corrected:
- PDF v7 on the drive (pages 3, 14 and 15)

Not yet corrected:
- Deck v4, slides 6 and 9
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday to our 34 Brussels contacts, which says 2.1. The embargo lifts Thursday at 10:00.

TUESDAY

1. Hanna, first thing. The press release is the only wrong thing that is already outside the building, so it comes before everything else. Assume she has heard nothing from me about this. She needs to send a corrected release to all 34 contacts, with one plain sentence saying the 2030 figure is 1.4 and not 2.1, and it should go out tomorrow, not Wednesday. If she wants a senior name on it, Geert can sign off. He knows I am away.

2. Check with Hanna which PDF the journalists received. If it was anything before v7, they need v7 as well. Please also make sure v7 is the only version that goes anywhere on Thursday, online or on paper.

3. Write to Tomás in Lindqvist's office. He emailed this morning and I have not answered. Three things:
- You are presenting and sitting on the panel instead of me.
- Yes to his new timings (see Thursday below).
- He needs the final names from our side by Wednesday 12:00 at the latest, otherwise security will not let people in. That is you instead of me, plus whoever else from the institute is coming. Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is bringing a colleague and I don't have the name. Please ask her, and check with Tomás whether the two of them are on his list or ours.

One question for him: the MEP now has to leave at 13:30 for a vote. Who chairs after that, or does the event end when she goes? The old run of show had Q&A until 14:00 and I don't know what he has in mind.

4. The deck. Slides 6 and 9 need the 1.4, including the revenue chart on 9. Look at my speaker notes on those two slides as well; I expect they still say 2.1. The presentation is now 15 minutes instead of 20, so something has to go. You made this deck, so cut what you would cut. My notes are only my notes. Throw out whatever doesn't sound like you.

WEDNESDAY

5. 12:00 is the deadline for the names to Tomás.

6. The press calls at 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each. One is a trade newsletter and one a Belgian daily. Hanna promised them me, so she needs to tell them it will be you. In my calendar they still say "Hanna to confirm", so please ask her whether the times are fixed. Both journalists will have read the release with 2.1 in it. I would bring up the correction yourself in the first minute, before they ask: old run, free allocation phase-out not applied, the right number is 1.4, the conclusion stands. Then move on to what the paper says.

THURSDAY

10:00 the embargo lifts.
12:00 guests have to be at the security entrance of the Altiero Spinelli building. Tomás collects the badges. There is a light lunch outside the room.
12:30 welcome by Lindqvist, 5 minutes.
12:35 your presentation, 15 minutes.
12:50 panel: Abena (remote), Kessler and you, with Lindqvist moderating. She wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves at 13:30.
After 13:30: whatever Tomás answers.

Two small things for the day. Ask someone to take photos and to count the room. Lucy needs two photos and the attendance numbers for their grant report by 4 December, and it is easy to forget when you are the one on stage.

KESSLER

He will try to make the whole panel about the 80% pass-through. His written comments are in this folder and he says there that he will raise it. Don't let him set the tone. You ran those sensitivity runs yourself, so this is your ground, not his.

- 80% is the central case. Annex B runs 40% and 60%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly, and say it before he does if you can. Once you have said it yourself he has very little left.
- Resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk. It is in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission's monitoring report.
- Abena will probably back us on the LDC side. She was strong on the call.

He may also try to use the corrected number against us. If he does, use the same sentence as with the journalists and add that the mistake was mine. Don't apologise for it more than once. A think tank that corrects its own figure before the launch is doing its job.

My reply lines from 13 November are in the folder too, but you don't need them. Everything in them is above.

WHO TO GO TO

- Hanna: anything about press, the release, the calls.
- Geert: sign-off, and anything you would rather not decide alone.
- Tomás: room, badges, timings, the MEP.
- Me: by phone, with the limits above.

LAST THING

In Lisbon the projector died in the middle of my panel and you got up and rescued it, with no slides and no warning. I have not forgotten that. You are better live than you think you are, and on Thursday you will have slides, three days and a paper you know inside out.

I trust you completely with this, including the decisions I haven't thought of. Whatever you decide on the day is the right call, and I will stand behind it.

Thank you, Inês. And once more, I am sorry.

Marieke
